STEP 1 - Vessel type: square flat plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plates are 20-30 cm; this one looks medium-large, around 23-25 cm.
b) Reference: a slice of bread is about 11 cm long. The bread slice spans roughly 0.9 of the plate's visible half-width, and the plate's width is about 2.2 bread-slice lengths across (the plate runs from x≈190 to x≈620 in the image, about 430 px, while the bread wedge is about 215 px long). So width ≈ 2.2 × 11 ≈ 24 cm.
Reconciled width: 24 cm (square), area = 576 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Bread: one wedge, roughly a quarter-to-third of a slice. Estimate about 0.6 of a slice = 0.6 × 30 g ≈ 20 g... but the wedge looks closer to a full thick slice segment, so take 1 slice-equivalent = 30 g.
- Watermelon: 6 visible cubes, roughly 3-4 cm each. Chunks are a single layer, so count them as pieces: each about 4 cm × 3 cm × 3 cm ≈ 36 ml at bulk density 0.6 g/ml ≈ 22 g... that gives about 22 g per cube is too high for typical cubes; use the footprint method instead. Watermelon footprint: about 6 cubes covering roughly 60 cm² total at 2.5 cm average thickness ≈ 150 ml × 0.6 = 90 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer or hidden food visible; the plate is flat.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:
- Bread (whole-grain/seeded, as served): about 250 kcal/100 g.
- Watermelon: about 30 kcal/100 g.

Totals: bread 30 g → 75 kcal; watermelon 90 g → 27 kcal. Total food ≈ 120 g, ≈ 102 kcal.
